papers.title: Processing enhances the anti-hepatocellular carcinoma effect of Momordicae Semen via remodeling chemical composition and regulating the Akt/mTOR/STAT3 pathway.
papers.abstract: Momordicae Semen (MS) is a traditional medicinal herb with reported antitumor potential. However, the impact of processing on its chemical composition and the underlying mechanisms against hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) remain insufficiently understood. This study aimed to characterize processing-induced chemical changes and elucidate the bioactive constituents and molecular pathways responsible for improved anti-HCC effects. UPLC-QTOF/MS was used to compare chemical differences between crude and processed samples. Network pharmacology, molecular docking, and molecular dynamics (MD) simulation
papers.summary: This study shows that processing Momordicae Semen (a traditional medicinal herb) enhances its anti-liver-cancer effects by altering its chemical composition. The processed extract appears to work by regulating the Akt/mTOR/STAT3 signaling pathway, and the study identifies key bioactive compounds through network pharmacology and molecular simulations.

papers.title: Garcinoic acid promotes ferroptosis-associated growth inhibition in esophageal squamous cell carcinoma through an MDM2-associated mechanism.
papers.abstract: Garcinoic acid (GA), a plant metabolite, has been shown to exhibit anti-inflammatory and antioxidant activities; however, its mechanism of action against esophageal squamous cell carcinoma (ESCC) remains unclear. This study aimed to investigate the effects of GA on ESCC and to elucidate its underlying molecular mechanisms.
papers.summary: This study investigates the anti-cancer effects of garcinoic acid (GA), a plant metabolite, on esophageal squamous cell carcinoma (ESCC). The findings reveal that GA promotes ferroptosis-associated growth inhibition through an MDM2-associated mechanism, providing a potential therapeutic avenue for ESCC.

papers.title: Comparative Structure-Based Analysis of Predicted BZD9L1 Binding Modes Across Human Sirtuins.
papers.abstract: Sirtuins (SIRTs) are NAD+-dependent enzymes implicated in cancer and other diseases, but the high conservation of their catalytic sites complicates the development of isoform-selective inhibitors. BZD9L1 is a benzimidazole-based sirtuin inhibitor with previously reported activity against SIRT1 and SIRT2. However, its potential interactions with other human sirtuin isoforms remain incompletely characterized. Here, we applied a comparative structure-based modelling framework integrating homology modelling, molecular docking, and targeted experimental assessment to investigate plausible binding m
papers.summary: This study uses computational modeling and experimental validation to predict how the sirtuin inhibitor BZD9L1 binds to different human sirtuin isoforms, revealing potential interactions beyond SIRT1/2. The findings may inform the design of more isoform-selective sirtuin inhibitors for cancer therapy.

papers.title: Identification of Natural Flavonoids Targeting PLK-1 as Potential Anti-Metastatic Agents: A Computational Approach.
papers.abstract: This study combines ligand- and structure-based in silico strategies to predict the inhibitory activity of natural flavonoids on the Polo-Like Kinase-1 (PLK-1) enzyme as candidate anticancer agents. This enzyme participates in mitosis and is overexpressed in cancer cells. Furthermore, it has been shown to have important implications for tumor metastasis, and its inhibitors are attractive starting points for drug development. First, classification models are developed using linear discriminant analysis and a multilayer perceptron neural network. Models with accuracy greater than 80%, validated
papers.summary: This study uses computational methods to identify natural flavonoids that may inhibit PLK-1, an enzyme overexpressed in cancer and linked to metastasis. The authors developed classification models with high accuracy to predict inhibitory activity, suggesting these compounds as potential anti-metastatic drug leads.

papers.title: Molecular Mechanisms of Foreign Body Responses to Neural Electrodes and Surface Biofunctionalization Strategies for Interface Modulation.
papers.abstract: Long-term implantable neural electrodes underpin brain-machine interfaces, deep brain stimulation, epilepsy monitoring, and closed-loop neuromodulation. Following chronic implantation, however, the foreign body response (FBR) at the electrode-tissue interface remains a major constraint on long-term performance, as reflected by increased interfacial impedance, lower signal-to-noise ratios, fewer resolvable units, and higher stimulation thresholds. This deterioration arises from interrelated events that include implantation injury, protein adsorption, blood-brain barrier disruption, complement a
papers.summary: This review examines the molecular mechanisms underlying the foreign body response (FBR) to chronic neural electrode implants, which degrades their performance over time. It also discusses surface biofunctionalization strategies aimed at modulating the electrode-tissue interface to improve long-term biocompatibility and functionality.

papers.title: CdS-Based Photocatalysts for Antimicrobial Applications: From Quantum Dots to Z-Scheme Heterojunctions-Mechanisms, Challenges, and Future Perspectives.
papers.abstract: The chronic overuse of antibiotics has accelerated the emergence of antibiotic-resistant bacteria, creating a global public health crisis as conventional therapies fail against multidrug-resistant pathogens spreading through water and food chains. Cadmium sulfide (CdS) has been established as an important visible-light-driven photocatalyst for antibacterial applications. This brief review systematically examines the structure-property relationships governing CdS-based antibacterial materials, including crystallographic polymorphs (cubic sphalerite and hexagonal wurtzite), morphological diversi
papers.summary: This review examines cadmium sulfide (CdS)-based photocatalysts for antibacterial applications, covering their mechanisms, structural variants from quantum dots to Z-scheme heterojunctions, and current challenges. It highlights the potential of these materials as a visible-light-driven alternative to conventional antibiotics against drug-resistant bacteria.

papers.title: FDA-Approved Drug Repurposing as p53 Mutants Rescue Candidates Using Structure-Based Virtual Screening and Molecular Simulations.
papers.abstract: The restoration of mutant p53 stability is a highly sought-after strategy in targeted cancer therapy. This study presents a structure-based virtual screening and molecular dynamics approach to nominate FDA-approved drugs as candidate stabilizers of mutant p53 for downstream experimental validation. A virtual screening library of FDA-approved compounds was docked against three representative p53 mutants (7DHY, 7DHZ, and 7V97) to evaluate their binding potential. The prioritized candidates demonstrated consistent, multi-conformer binding affinities. Protein-ligand interaction profiling revealed
papers.summary: This study uses structure-based virtual screening and molecular dynamics to identify FDA-approved drugs that could stabilize mutant p53, a key target in cancer therapy. The authors docked a library of approved compounds against three p53 mutants and prioritized candidates with consistent binding affinities and favorable interaction profiles, providing a shortlist for experimental validation.

papers.title: Solvent Interaction Analysis: A New Lens for Protein Structure and Diagnostics.
papers.abstract: Aqueous two-phase systems (ATPSs) provide a versatile, fully aqueous platform for probing solute-water interactions and protein structure. This review first surveys the diversity and phase behavior of biphasic aqueous systems formed by polymers and salts. We describe how phase diagrams characterize ATPS formation and composition and how both polymer chemistry and salt identity, rather than molecular size alone, govern phase separation by modulating the solvent properties of water. Building on a modified binodal model, we show that phase separation and solute partitioning can be understood in t
papers.summary: This review highlights aqueous two-phase systems (ATPSs) as a versatile platform for studying protein-solvent interactions and protein structure. It emphasizes that polymer chemistry and salt identity, not just molecular size, govern phase separation by modulating water's solvent properties, and proposes a modified binodal model to understand solute partitioning. The work offers a new conceptual lens for protein diagnostics and structural analysis.

papers.title: Identification and functional characterization of a SUZ12 frameshift variant in a Chinese family with Imagawa-Matsumoto syndrome.
papers.abstract: Imagawa-Matsumoto syndrome (IMMAS) is a rare overgrowth disorder caused by heterozygous loss-of-function variants in SUZ12, which encodes a core subunit of the Polycomb Repressive Complex 2 (PRC2). To date, fewer than 20 cases have been reported, and the molecular mechanisms underlying PRC2 dysfunction in IMMAS remain incompletely understood.
papers.summary: This study identifies and functionally characterizes a novel SUZ12 frameshift variant in a Chinese family with Imagawa-Matsumoto syndrome (IMMAS), a rare overgrowth disorder. The findings expand the known mutational spectrum of SUZ12 and provide functional evidence linking the variant to PRC2 dysfunction, improving understanding of the molecular basis of IMMAS.

papers.title: Molecular Dynamics and Electron Density Topology Reveal Ligand-Specific Interaction Patterns at the Dopamine D2 Receptor.
papers.abstract: The dopamine D2 receptor (D2R) is one of the principal therapeutic targets for the treatment of schizophrenia and other neuropsychiatric disorders. Understanding how ligands with different pharmacological profiles interact with D2R is essential for the rational design of safer and more effective antipsychotic drugs. In this work, Molecular Dynamics (MD) simulations combined with Quantum Theory of Atoms in Molecules (QTAIM) analysis were employed to investigate the electronic nature of protein-ligand interactions in D2R embedded in a neuronal membrane environment. Representative agonists (dopam
papers.summary: This study uses molecular dynamics simulations combined with quantum theory of atoms in molecules (QTAIM) analysis to reveal ligand-specific electronic interaction patterns at the dopamine D2 receptor, a key target for antipsychotic drugs. The findings provide atomic-level insights into how agonists and other ligands interact with the receptor in a neuronal membrane environment, which could inform the rational design of safer and more effective antipsychotics.

papers.title: Linear Residual Network Modeling for Anti-HIV-1 Activity Prediction and Docking-Validated Design of Biphenyl-DAPY-Based NNRTIs.
papers.abstract: To predict the anti-HIV-1 activity of biphenyl-DAPY-based non-nucleoside reverse transcriptase inhibitors (NNRTIs), a quantitative structure-activity relationship (QSAR) analysis was conducted. Using the heuristic method (HM) for descriptor selection, four predictive models were established: support vector regression (SVR), kernel ridge regression, linear mixed-kernel SVR, and Linear Residual Network (LRNet). Rigorous validations, including leave-one-out cross-validation, fivefold cross-validation, and Y-randomization tests, confirmed their reliability. The LRNet model exhibited the best perfo
papers.summary: This study develops QSAR models, including a Linear Residual Network (LRNet), to predict anti-HIV-1 activity of biphenyl-DAPY-based NNRTIs. The LRNet model outperformed other methods and was used with docking to design new inhibitors with improved predicted activity.

papers.title: Novel 6-aryl-1-(3,4,5-trimethoxyphenyl)-1H-pyrazolo[3,4-d]pyrimidine derivatives: design, synthesis, and biological evaluation as potent tubulin polymerisation inhibitors with anticancer activity.
papers.abstract: Microtubules assembled from α/β-tubulin heterodimers are critical for cell division and well-established anticancer drug targets, making tubulin polymerization inhibitors a viable route for new chemotherapeutics. Guided by structural analysis of colchicine-site binders and tubulin-ligand computational simulations, we rationally designed and synthesized a series of 6-aryl-1-(3,4,5-trimethoxyphenyl)-1H-pyrazolo[3,4-d]pyrimidines as novel colchicine-binding site tubulin inhibitors. Derivative 9t displayed the strongest antiproliferative potency, with IC₅。 values of 0.065-0.096 μM across tested ca
papers.journal: Journal of enzyme inhibition and medicinal chemistry
papers.summary: This study reports the design and synthesis of novel pyrazolo[3,4-d]pyrimidine derivatives as colchicine-site tubulin polymerization inhibitors, guided by computational modeling. The lead compound 9t showed potent antiproliferative activity with IC50 values in the sub-micromolar range, highlighting its potential as a new anticancer chemotherapeutic.

papers.title: A systematic evaluation framework for universal antibody-antigen binding affinity prediction and candidate recommendation.
papers.abstract: Predicting antigen-antibody binding is essential to drug discovery and protein engineering. For de novo antibody design, generalizable binding prediction models are crucial for efficient in silico screening. However, existing affinity predictors lack generalization, with performance deteriorating for antibodies targeting antigens absent from training data or datasets lacking non-binders. To address this, we establish a benchmarking framework for evaluating universal antibody-antigen binding affinity prediction. Our framework compares sequence- and structure-based methods across diverse antigen
papers.summary: This paper introduces a benchmarking framework to systematically evaluate universal antibody-antigen binding affinity prediction methods, addressing the lack of generalization in existing predictors for unseen antigens and datasets without non-binders. The framework compares sequence- and structure-based approaches across diverse antigens, providing a standardized evaluation to guide model selection and development for in silico antibody screening.

papers.title: Sabinene attenuates inflammation and oxidative stress in CFA-induced arthritis: In vivo and in silico evidence implicating TLR4/NLRP3/NF-κB signaling.
papers.abstract: Rheumatoid arthritis (RA) is a chronic immune-mediated disease in which persistent inflammation and oxidative stress contribute to progressive joint damage. This study evaluated the prophylactic effects of sabinene in complete Freund's adjuvant (CFA)-induced arthritis and explored potential molecular associations using integrated in vivo and computational approaches. Rats were allocated to vehicle control, arthritic control, piroxicam, or sabinene groups (15, 30, or 60 mg/kg; n = 6/group); sabinene was administered orally beginning 30 minutes before CFA injection and continued for 28 days. Paw
papers.summary: This study demonstrates that sabinene, a natural monoterpene, reduces inflammation and oxidative stress in a rat model of rheumatoid arthritis, with effects comparable to the standard drug piroxicam. Using in vivo experiments and computational modeling, the authors implicate the TLR4/NLRP3/NF-κB signaling pathway as a key mediator of sabinene's anti-arthritic activity.

papers.title: An integrated approach: green extraction technique optimization, mechanistic study, and bioactivity profiling of four flavonoids from Epimedium sagittatum.
papers.abstract: In this study, a novel strategy for simultaneous extraction of four key flavonoids (epimedin A, epimedin B, epimedin C, and icariin) from Epimedium sagittatum using deep eutectic solvent-ultrasound assisted extraction (DES-UAE) was developed. Initially, 24 kinds of DESs were produced, a proline-lactic acid system demonstrated optimal extraction efficiency. The ideal parameters were established by single-factor experiments and response surface methodology optimization: water content of 29%, molar ratio of 1 : 1.9, liquid-solid ratio of 32 : 1 mL g-1, ultrasound power of 280 W and extraction tim
papers.summary: This study develops an optimized green extraction method using deep eutectic solvents combined with ultrasound to efficiently extract four bioactive flavonoids from Epimedium sagittatum, identifying a proline-lactic acid system as most effective. The work includes mechanistic insights and bioactivity profiling, offering a sustainable alternative for natural product extraction.

papers.title: In silico, in vitro, and in vivo evaluation of the antiviral potential of glycyrrhizic acid and chitosan nanoparticles against foot and mouth disease virus.
papers.abstract: Foot-and-mouth disease (FMD) considers as one of the extremely infectious diseases with major economic impact on cloven-hoofed animals globally. The causative agent of the disease, Foot and Mouth Disease Virus (FMDV), comprises seven serotypes designated as; O, A, SAT1, SAT2, SAT3, C, and Asia1. Over the past decades, studies have shown that glycyrrhizic acid, the primary bioactive compound of licorice root, and chitosan, as a biodegradable and biocompatible natural polymer derived from crustacean shells, are potent candidates for inhibition of FMDV activity. The current work evaluated the pot
papers.summary: This study evaluates the antiviral potential of glycyrrhizic acid and chitosan nanoparticles against foot-and-mouth disease virus (FMDV) using in silico, in vitro, and in vivo approaches. The findings suggest these compounds may inhibit FMDV activity, offering a potential therapeutic strategy against this economically devastating livestock disease.

papers.title: Glycoconjugate strategy for GLUT-driven curcumin delivery and anticancer activity in breast cancer cells.
papers.abstract: Selective targeting of cancer cells is a critical strategy in anticancer therapy, and the overexpression of glucose transporters (GLUTs) in malignant cells provides an attractive avenue for achieving this selectivity. In this study, we report the synthesis and biological evaluation of glycoconjugate vanadyl complexes as GLUT-directed anticancer agents against breast cancer. A Schiff base ligand (CG) was synthesized through the condensation of curcumin (C) and glucosamine (G), followed by complexation with vanadyl to form [VO(CG)₂]·5H₂O. The synthesized compounds were comprehensively characteri
papers.summary: This study describes the synthesis of a curcumin-glucosamine conjugate and its vanadyl complex, designed to exploit GLUT overexpression for targeted delivery to breast cancer cells. The glycoconjugate strategy aims to enhance selective anticancer activity, with the compounds characterized and evaluated for biological effects.

papers.title: Discovery of Novel Druggable Binding Pockets on SARS-CoV-2 PLpro via Fragment Screening and Insights for Structure-Based Inhibitor Design.
papers.abstract: Coronaviruses are a large family of viruses capable of causing severe respiratory diseases, with recent outbreaks posing major threats to global public health. The SARS-CoV-2 papain-like protease (PLpro) is an essential viral enzyme involved in viral replication and host immune evasion, making it an attractive target for antiviral drug development. However, no PLpro-targeted drugs have yet been approved. Here, we employed a fragment-based drug discovery (FBDD) strategy combined with crystallographic screening and identified 23 fragment compounds with well-defined electron density. These fragme
papers.summary: This study used fragment-based drug discovery and crystallographic screening to identify 23 fragment compounds binding to novel druggable pockets on the SARS-CoV-2 papain-like protease (PLpro), an essential antiviral target. The findings provide new structural insights and a starting point for designing PLpro-targeted inhibitors, potentially advancing COVID-19 therapeutics.

papers.title: Integrated computational and preclinical evaluation of drug repurposing candidates for KRAS-mutant non-small cell lung cancer.
papers.abstract: KRAS mutations, particularly KRAS G12C, pose significant therapeutic challenges in non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) due to limited inhibitor efficacy and rapid resistance. Drug repurposing offers a time and cost-effective strategy to identify alternative therapeutic options targeting KRAS-driven signalling. A structure-based drug repurposing approach was employed to screen FDA-approved compounds targeting key regulators to the MAPK signalling pathway and computationally modelled for potential engagement with the KRAS G12C switch-II pocket. Computational analyses including virtual screening,
papers.summary: This study uses a structure-based drug repurposing approach to screen FDA-approved compounds for potential binding to the KRAS G12C switch-II pocket, aiming to identify alternative therapeutic options for KRAS-mutant non-small cell lung cancer. The computational predictions are integrated with preclinical evaluations, offering a time- and cost-effective strategy to overcome limited inhibitor efficacy and resistance.

papers.title: Discovery of a potent TDP1 inhibitor through machine learning-driven predictive modeling combined with structure-based virtual screening and experimental validation.
papers.abstract: Tyrosyl-DNA phosphodiesterase I (TDP1) repairs topoisomerase I (TOP1)-mediated DNA damage and is a promising anticancer target, particularly in combination with TOP1 inhibitors. However, the discovery of potent and drug-like TDP1 inhibitors remains challenging due to the limited structural diversity of known active compounds. Here, we developed an integrated computational framework combining machine learning (ML), deep learning (DL), and structure-based docking with experimental validation. A curated dataset of 2040 compounds (857 active, 1183 inactive) was assembled and analyzed by scaffold c
papers.summary: This study presents an integrated computational pipeline combining machine learning, deep learning, and structure-based virtual screening to identify novel TDP1 inhibitors, a promising anticancer target. The approach successfully discovered a potent inhibitor with experimental validation, addressing the limited structural diversity of known active compounds.

papers.title: On Void Formation during the Simulated Tensile Testing of Polymer-Filler Particle Composites.
papers.abstract: We simulate model polymer composites composed of linear polymer strands and spherical, monodisperse filler particles (FP). These molecular dynamics simulations implement a coarse-grained, bead-spring force field, and we vary several formulation parameters to study their influences on material properties. These parameters include FP radius, FP volume fraction, temperature, and the polymer-polymer, FP-FP, and polymer-FP interaction potentials. Uniaxial extension of the simulation cells allows direct comparison of the mechanical reinforcement (or weakening) provided by the FP. We focus on the for
papers.summary: This study uses molecular dynamics simulations to investigate how filler particle size, volume fraction, temperature, and interaction strengths affect void formation and mechanical properties in polymer composites during tensile testing. The findings provide insights into the mechanisms of reinforcement or weakening, which could inform the design of stronger composite materials.

papers.title: Nitrogen Fixation by MoSn3 and MoSn5 Clusters.
papers.abstract: The Haber-Bosch process (HBP) for the conversion of nitrogen into ammonia is arguably one of the most important chemical reactions in human history because it is the basis for the large-scale production of fertilizers and hence of global food production. Nevertheless, the HBP contributes in a decisive manner to the production of CO2 and other global warming gases, since it is an extremely energy-intensive process. Consequently, the development of alternative conditions to reduce its negative environmental impact is of the highest priority. In this study, we investigate the detailed mechanism o
papers.summary: This computational study investigates the mechanism of nitrogen fixation by MoSn3 and MoSn5 clusters, proposing them as potential alternatives to the energy-intensive Haber-Bosch process. The findings provide detailed mechanistic insights that could inform the design of more sustainable catalysts for ammonia production.

papers.title: Rational design, synthesis, and antimicrobial evaluation of novel 1,2,3-triazole hybrids: structure-activity relationships, molecular docking, and DFT studies.
papers.abstract: A series of novel 2,4-dichlorophenyl-1,2,3-triazole derivatives and their structural hybrids incorporating chalcone, hydrazone, thio/semicarbazide, carbamate, and pyrazole moieties were rationally designed, synthesized, and characterized. The antimicrobial activity of the synthesized compounds was evaluated against Gram-positive and Gram-negative bacteria, as well as Candida albicans, revealing clear structure-dependent activity profiles. Among the tested compounds, the parent triazole-acetyl scaffold (compound 3) exhibited the most consistent broad-spectrum activity, with MIC values of 22.5 m
papers.summary: This study reports the rational design and synthesis of novel 1,2,3-triazole hybrids with various structural moieties, evaluating their antimicrobial activity against bacteria and Candida albicans. The parent triazole-acetyl scaffold showed the most consistent broad-spectrum activity, and structure-activity relationships were supported by molecular docking and DFT studies.

papers.title: Sparsomycin inhibits translation through a conserved mechanism across all domains of life.
papers.abstract: Sparsomycin (SPA) is a broad-spectrum inhibitor of protein synthesis with activity across all three domains of life. Although SPA has long been known to target the ribosomal peptidyl transferase center (PTC), previous structural studies suggested that SPA binds differently to bacterial ribosomes compared to their archaeal and eukaryotic counterparts-an unexpected conclusion given the high evolutionary conservation of the ribosomal catalytic center. Here, we show that SPA inhibits a majority of elongation-competent bacterial ribosomal complexes and present X-ray crystal structures of Thermus th
papers.summary: This study reveals that the antibiotic sparsomycin inhibits protein synthesis through a conserved mechanism across all domains of life, contrary to previous suggestions of domain-specific binding. Using X-ray crystallography and biochemical assays, the authors show that sparsomycin binds uniformly to the ribosomal peptidyl transferase center, resolving a long-standing discrepancy and reinforcing the evolutionary conservation of the ribosome's catalytic core.

papers.title: Systematic mapping of insertion-tolerant regions enables capsid engineering of an infectious RNA phage.
papers.abstract: RNA phages are attractive platforms for the design of programmable bioparticles, but their development has been constrained by limited knowledge of genomic sites that can tolerate sequence insertion. Here, we combined MuA transposase-mediated in vitro insertion mutagenesis with our established reverse genetics systems to systematically identify insertion-tolerant regions (ITRs) in the RNA phages MS2 and PP7. Screening of 4,555 MS2 and 2,228 PP7 random insertion clones identified 29 and 26 non-redundant ITRs, respectively. We further analyzed and compared these ITRs in the context of RNA genome
papers.summary: This study systematically maps insertion-tolerant regions (ITRs) in the genomes of RNA phages MS2 and PP7 using transposon-mediated mutagenesis and reverse genetics, identifying 29 and 26 non-redundant ITRs, respectively. These ITRs provide a roadmap for engineering programmable bioparticles by enabling targeted insertions of foreign sequences without disrupting phage viability.

papers.title: Determinants of substrate specificity in mint pulegone reductase, a double bond reductase of the medium-chain dehydrogenase/reductase superfamily.
papers.abstract: Pulegone reductase from peppermint (Mentha × piperita; MpPulR) is an NADPH-dependent medium-chain dehydrogenase/reductase that catalyzes asymmetric reduction of the C4-C7 double bond of (+)-pulegone to (-)-menthone and (+)-isomenthone. To define the structural determinants of substrate recognition and catalytic turnover, we integrated structure-based modeling (docking and molecular dynamics (MD) simulations) with experimental mutagenesis and comprehensive substrate profiling. Residues positioned closely to (+)-pulegone in homology-based structural models were subjected to L-Ala-scanning mutage
papers.summary: This study identifies key amino acid residues in mint pulegone reductase that determine substrate specificity and catalytic activity, using a combination of structural modeling, molecular dynamics simulations, and mutagenesis. The findings provide insights into the enzyme's substrate recognition mechanism, which could inform engineering of double bond reductases for biotechnological applications.

papers.title: Multifunctional Near-Infrared-Responsive Silk Fibroin Nanomedicine for Tumor Treatment and Imaging.
papers.abstract: The complexity and heterogeneity of tumors make monotherapy inadequate for effective tumor elimination, highlighting the urgent need for multifunctional synergistic therapeutic strategies. In this study, a near-infrared (NIR)-responsive multimodal therapeutic nanoplatform (FSINPs) was constructed by simple adsorption of indocyanine green (ICG) and Fe3+ onto silk fibroin nanoparticles. Molecular docking showed that ICG binds stably to silk fibroin mainly via hydrogen bonds. Density functional theory (DFT) calculations predicted that Fe3+ strongly coordinates with the sulfonate groups of ICG and
papers.summary: This study develops a multifunctional silk fibroin-based nanoplatform that responds to near-infrared light for combined tumor imaging and therapy, leveraging ICG and Fe3+ for photothermal and photodynamic effects. The work demonstrates a promising synergistic strategy to overcome the limitations of monotherapy in cancer treatment.

papers.title: Novel tetrazole annulation on benzopyridodiazepine derivatives as inhibitor of tropomyosin kinase B (TrkB): rational design, synthesis, biological evaluation, SAR, and in silico studies.
papers.abstract: Tropomyosin kinase B (TrkB) is an attractive target for cancer treatment and is emerging as a target for the treatment of neurological disorders, specifically epilepsy, due to its role in regulating neuronal degeneration and inflammation. However, current medications frequently suffer from toxicity, resistance, and poor metabolism. In the present study, four new series of tetrazole annulated benzopyridodiazepine derivatives (26 examples) were synthesized in two steps: intramolecular cyclization with various sets of amines to produce benzopyridodiazepinone derivatives, and then, in the second s
papers.summary: This study describes the design and synthesis of 26 novel tetrazole-annulated benzopyridodiazepine derivatives as potential inhibitors of tropomyosin kinase B (TrkB), a target for cancer and neurological disorders. The compounds were evaluated for biological activity, structure-activity relationships, and in silico properties, aiming to overcome issues like toxicity and resistance in current treatments.

papers.title: Stabilization of prefusion hMPV F improves manufacturability and protective immunity across hMPV lineages.
papers.abstract: Human metapneumovirus (hMPV) is a major cause of pediatric acute lower respiratory tract infections (ALRTIs), yet vaccine development has been hindered by the intrinsic metastability of the prefusion F glycoprotein (pre-F). Here, we used a structure-based design strategy to stabilize hMPV pre-F while preserving neutralization-sensitive epitopes. By applying combined stabilizing elements, including disulfide bonds, a designed salt bridge, and a trimer-interface sequence swap, we generated VM-874, a pre-F-stabilized trimer that was expressed at high levels in 293F cells and exhibited improved th
papers.summary: This study describes a structure-based design approach to stabilize the prefusion F glycoprotein of human metapneumovirus (hMPV), generating a variant called VM-874 that is expressed at high levels and retains neutralization-sensitive epitopes. The stabilized pre-F trimer improves manufacturability and elicits protective immunity across hMPV lineages, addressing a key barrier in vaccine development.

papers.title: Multi-Scale Characterization of Interfacial Adhesion and Material Selection for Crack Sealants in High-Altitude Airport Asphalt Pavements.
papers.abstract: Asphalt pavements at high-altitude airports endure prolonged extreme low temperatures and large diurnal swings, imposing stringent demands on crack sealants, whose multi-scale adhesion failure mechanism remains unclear. Three SBS and crumb-rubber-composite-modified sealants, designated A, B and C, were characterized through surface free energy tests, pull-off and shear tests, fluorescence microscopy, FTIR and molecular dynamics simulations. Cross-scale correlation analysis and CRITIC-TOPSIS were applied to link and rank the sealants across scales. Work of cohesion, work of adhesion, pull-off s
papers.summary: This study characterizes three SBS and crumb-rubber-composite-modified crack sealants for high-altitude airport asphalt pavements using multi-scale methods, including surface free energy tests, mechanical tests, microscopy, FTIR, and molecular dynamics simulations. The authors identify interfacial adhesion failure mechanisms and use CRITIC-TOPSIS analysis to rank the sealants, providing a framework for material selection in extreme low-temperature environments.

papers.title: Broad-Spectrum Multi-Epitope Design Targeting Conserved Hantavirus Glycoproteins (Gn/Gc): Chimeric Antigen Engineering and Structural Mapping.
papers.abstract: Hantaviruses, the etiological agents of hemorrhagic fever with renal syndrome (HFRS) and hantavirus pulmonary syndrome (HPS), represent a high-risk zoonotic threat with substantial global health impact. Currently, there is no FDA-approved vaccine. The viral surface glycoprotein (GP) is crucial for host cell entry and is regarded as a key target for vaccine development. However, its variability among hantavirus species limits the effectiveness of conventional vaccine strategies. Epitope-based vaccines offer a promising alternative by enabling the design of broadly protective constructs. In this
papers.summary: This study presents a computational design of a broad-spectrum multi-epitope vaccine targeting conserved regions of hantavirus glycoproteins (Gn/Gc), using chimeric antigen engineering and structural mapping to address viral variability. The approach aims to overcome the lack of an FDA-approved vaccine by focusing on conserved epitopes that could provide cross-protection against multiple hantavirus species.

papers.title: Physicochemical, Rheological, and Sensory Characterization of Gluten-Reduced Cookies Enriched with Amaranth and Chickpea Flours.
papers.abstract: The global transition toward plant-based diets necessitates the development of sustainable, nutritionally enriched, and gluten-reduced bakery products. This study evaluated the techno-functional, nutritional, and sensory impacts of substituting wheat flour at levels of 30%, 50%, and 70% with a binary blend of amaranth (Amaranthus caudatus) and chickpea (Cicer arietinum) flours in short-dough cookies. Dough's thermo-mechanical behavior was characterized using the Mixolab Chopin+ protocol and correlated with Texture Profile Analysis (TPA) and consumer acceptability (n = 60) via Principal Compone
papers.summary: This study investigates the effects of substituting wheat flour with amaranth and chickpea flours at 30%, 50%, and 70% levels in gluten-reduced cookies, evaluating dough thermo-mechanical properties, texture, and consumer acceptability. The findings provide insights into optimizing plant-based, gluten-reduced bakery products with improved nutritional profiles while maintaining sensory quality.

papers.title: Molecular Dynamics Study of Hydrogen Release from NaH Using Machine Learning Potential.
papers.abstract: Sodium hydride (NaH) is the main by-product generated during the operation of the cold traps in a sodium-cooled fast reactor. Its thermal decomposition releases hydrogen gas, posing a safety hazard. However, understanding the atomic-scale decomposition mechanism remains challenging because conventional simulation methods are limited in the accessible length and time scales. This study developed a deep neural network potential (DP) for the NaH system using the DP-GEN active learning framework. Benchmark tests show that the DP model accurately reproduces density functional theory (DFT) reference
papers.summary: This study developed a machine learning potential for sodium hydride (NaH) to simulate hydrogen release during thermal decomposition, overcoming the length and time scale limitations of conventional methods. The deep neural network potential accurately reproduces DFT reference data, enabling atomic-scale insights into the decomposition mechanism relevant to safety in sodium-cooled fast reactors.

papers.title: Effects of L-glutamic acid on wheat starch structure and functionality: multiscale characterization and molecular dynamics simulations.
papers.abstract: L-Glutamic acid (L-Glu) is central to carbon-nitrogen metabolism, yet its ability to improve starch quality by regulating grain metabolism and by directly modulating starch structure remains unclear. In this study, we integrated a field experiment with an in vitro experiment and combined untargeted metabolomics, microscopy, structural characterization, physicochemical and processing property analyses, and molecular dynamics simulations. It was found that under drought, L-Glu spraying reprogrammed the grain metabolome, with pathway enrichment in aminoacyl-tRNA biosynthesis and starch/sucrose me
papers.summary: This study shows that spraying L-glutamic acid on wheat under drought conditions improves starch quality by reprogramming grain metabolism and directly modifying starch structure, as revealed through integrated field and in vitro experiments with multiscale characterization and molecular dynamics simulations. The findings suggest L-glutamic acid could be used to enhance starch functionality in crops under stress.

papers.title: From in silico screening to experimental verification: Identification of novel umami peptides from tamarind (Tamarindus indica L.) seed proteins and their validation in enzymatic hydrolysates.
papers.abstract: Umami peptides are key contributors to food flavor enhancement. In this study, novel umami peptides from tamarind seed proteins were identified using an integrated strategy combining in silico screening and experimental validation. A virtual peptide library was screened based on physicochemical properties and bioactivity, yielding six candidates (VSDY, DGIDF, AKNVSDYL, YNDPHC, VPPD, and NDPHCQY). Molecular docking and dynamics simulations revealed stable binding to the umami receptor T1R1/T1R3 via hydrogen bonding and hydrophobic interactions, with binding affinities of -7.9 to -8.8 kcal/mol.
papers.summary: This study identified novel umami peptides from tamarind seed proteins using a combination of in silico screening and experimental validation. Six candidate peptides were found to bind stably to the umami receptor T1R1/T1R3, and their umami taste was confirmed in enzymatic hydrolysates, offering potential for natural flavor enhancement.

papers.title: Experimental, Genomic, and Structural Evidence Supporting Putative PET-Hydrolases in Thermophilic Bacteria Isolated From Hot Springs in Cajamarca, Peru.
papers.abstract: Polyethylene terephthalate (PET) waste represents a major environmental challenge due to limited recycling solutions. Thermophilic bacteria from geothermal environments harbor diverse enzymatic machinery adapted to extreme conditions, offering promising biocatalysts for plastic degradation; however, biological resources from Peru and other South American countries remain scarce. We characterized four bacterial strains isolated from two geothermal sites in Cajamarca, Peru, screened for PET hydrolysis at 50°C. Whole-genome sequencing using hybrid assembly achieved near-complete circular genomes.
papers.summary: This study characterizes four thermophilic bacterial strains from hot springs in Peru, using whole-genome sequencing to identify putative PET-hydrolase enzymes. The research provides experimental and structural evidence supporting their potential for plastic degradation at high temperatures, contributing new biological resources from an underexplored region.

papers.title: Synergistic H2─CH4 Co-Adsorption on Scandium-Decorated [5]Cycloparaphenylene Nanohoops for Gas Storage Application.
papers.abstract: This work presents computational insights into the cooperative adsorption and storage of hydrogen and methane gas in scandium (Sc) decorated [5]cycloparaphenylene ([5]CPP) nanohoops using first principles calculations supplemented with Grimme's dispersion correction (DFT+D3). The Sc atoms were functionalized over the [5]CPP molecule with an average binding energy of 1.53 eV. A single Sc atom can store up to five hydrogen molecules and four methane molecules in quasi-molecular form. The calculated average adsorption energies vary between 0.21 and 0.353 eV/H2 and 0.263 and 0.243 eV/CH4. At low t
papers.summary: This computational study explores the use of scandium-decorated [5]cycloparaphenylene nanohoops for storing hydrogen and methane gases. The authors find that each scandium atom can bind up to five H2 and four CH4 molecules with moderate adsorption energies, suggesting potential for gas storage applications.

papers.title: A destination-driven framework for nanoparticle-enabled targeted protein degradation.
papers.abstract: Targeted protein degradation (TPD) offers a revolutionary paradigm to eliminate disease-driving proteins. Given the distinct technical requirements and challenges associated with degrading intracellular versus extracellular proteins, we classify existing TPD strategies based on subcellular localization into two categories: intracellular TPD (iTPD), which targets proteins within the cytoplasm and nucleus, and extracellular TPD (eTPD), which focuses on membrane-bound and secreted proteins. This destination-based framework facilitates precise technology selection and rational design by aligning m
papers.summary: This review proposes a framework for classifying targeted protein degradation (TPD) strategies based on the subcellular destination of the target protein—intracellular (iTPD) versus extracellular (eTPD)—and discusses how nanoparticle-enabled approaches can be tailored to each category. The framework aims to guide technology selection and rational design for more effective protein degradation therapeutics.

papers.title: Tuning protein corona on nucleic acid nanodrugs for targeted delivery.
papers.abstract: Nanoparticle-based delivery systems hold transformative potential for nucleic acid therapeutics. However, the fate of nucleic acid nanodrugs (NANDs) in vivo differs significantly from that observed in vitro, directly impacting their therapeutic efficacy. Upon introduction into biological fluids, NANDs rapidly adsorb proteins onto their surfaces, forming an assembled adsorption layer known as the protein corona (PC). This PC critically influences the physicochemical properties of NANDs and consequently governs their subsequent biological interactions. This review comprehensively introduces the
papers.summary: This review discusses how the protein corona (PC) that forms on nucleic acid nanodrugs (NANDs) in biological fluids affects their behavior and therapeutic efficacy, and explores strategies to tune the PC for improved targeted delivery. It highlights the gap between in vitro and in vivo performance and the critical role of the PC in determining biological interactions.

papers.title: Edge-aware GAT-based protein binding sites prediction.
papers.abstract: Accurate identification of protein binding sites is crucial for understanding biomolecular interaction mechanisms and for the rational design of drug targets. Traditional predictive methods often struggle to balance prediction accuracy with computational efficiency when capturing complex spatial conformations. To address this challenge, we propose an Edge-aware Graph Attention Network (Edge-aware GAT) model for the fine-grained prediction of binding sites across various biomolecules, including proteins, DNA/RNA, ions, ligands, and lipids. Our method constructs atom-level graphs and integrates
papers.summary: This paper introduces an Edge-aware Graph Attention Network (GAT) for predicting protein binding sites across diverse biomolecules, including proteins, DNA/RNA, ions, ligands, and lipids. By constructing atom-level graphs and integrating edge features, the model improves prediction accuracy and computational efficiency compared to traditional methods.

papers.title: Geometric Deep Learning-Based Drug Design Models for Small-Molecule Drug Discovery.
papers.abstract: Deep neural network (DNN)-based in silico models show great promise in predicting the properties and bioactivities of novel compounds, including small molecules. Among traditional approaches, structure-based drug design (SBDD) remains a fundamental approach for drug discovery using molecular docking, scoring functions, and molecular dynamics simulations. However, these approaches are often constrained by limited flexibility, resolution, and generalizability. Geometric deep learning (GDL) offers a transformative alternative by enabling models to learn directly from non-Euclidean molecular repre
papers.summary: This review discusses how geometric deep learning (GDL) models are transforming small-molecule drug discovery by learning directly from non-Euclidean molecular representations, overcoming limitations of traditional structure-based approaches like docking and molecular dynamics. It highlights GDL's potential to improve property prediction and bioactivity assessment for novel compounds.

papers.title: Effects of different marine surimi addition on the gelling properties of freshwater surimi gels: Protein crosslinking and endogenous enzyme interactions.
papers.abstract: Blending freshwater and marine surimi has been widely applied to improve gel product quality, while the species-dependent effects on gelation remain unclear. This study evaluated the effects of Alaska pollock surimi and hairtail surimi on the gelation properties of silver carp surimi at different blending ratios (0-40%). Alaska pollock surimi enhanced gelation, increasing gel strength, hardness and whiteness. In contrast, hairtail surimi weakened gelation, reducing gel strength and whiteness. Water-state and structural analyses showed that hairtail surimi increased water mobility and generated
papers.summary: This study shows that blending freshwater silver carp surimi with different marine surimi species has opposite effects on gel quality: Alaska pollock surimi improves gel strength, hardness, and whiteness, while hairtail surimi weakens these properties. The differences are linked to species-specific protein crosslinking and endogenous enzyme activities, which alter water mobility and gel structure. These findings provide guidance for optimizing mixed-surimi formulations in the food industry.

papers.title: Computational investigation for exploring botanical ingredients as potential negative allosteric modulators targeting metabotropic glutamate receptor 5.
papers.abstract: Metabotropic glutamate receptors are class C G-protein-coupled receptors that respond to the neurotransmitter glutamate. In particular, metabotropic glutamate receptor 5 (mGluR5) has been a valuable drug target for the management of psychiatric and neurodegenerative disorders such as fragile X syndrome, autism, depression, anxiety, addiction, and movement disorders through negative allosteric modulators (NAMs). Despite the discovery of several NAMs, limited clinical efficacy was observed, thus preventing them from reaching the clinical stage. Natural products are indispensable, with a plethora
papers.summary: This study computationally screens botanical compounds as potential negative allosteric modulators (NAMs) of metabotropic glutamate receptor 5 (mGluR5), a drug target for psychiatric and neurodegenerative disorders. The findings identify promising natural product candidates that may overcome the limited clinical efficacy of existing NAMs.

papers.title: Identification and Validation of Mannose Metabolism-Related Biomarkers in COPD Through Integrated Bioinformatics and Machine Learning Analysis: A Pilot Study.
papers.abstract: Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) represents a progressive respiratory disorder marked by sustained airflow restriction and ongoing inflammatory processes. Recently, mannose metabolism has emerged as a significant factor in chronic disease development. This investigation explored how mannose metabolism-related genes (MMRGs) contribute to COPD pathogenesis and evaluated their utility as candidate diagnostic and therapeutic targets.
papers.journal: International journal of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease
papers.summary: This pilot study uses integrated bioinformatics and machine learning to identify mannose metabolism-related genes as potential biomarkers for COPD, a progressive respiratory disease. The findings suggest these genes may serve as diagnostic and therapeutic targets, though further validation is needed.

papers.title: UNKAI: A Protein Functional Identity Prediction Model Based on ESM-C Latent Representations and the Attention Mechanism.
papers.abstract: The rapid advancement of genome sequencing technologies has led to the accumulation of a vast number of protein sequences in public databases. However, a substantial proportion of these proteins remain functionally uncharacterized. Concurrently, the expansion of protein sequence data has enabled the development of protein language models (pLMs). By distilling billions of years of evolutionary history into a latent representational space, these models have acquired an unprecedented capacity to predict both the tertiary structures and functions of proteins. In this study, we developed a deep lea
papers.summary: The authors developed UNKAI, a deep learning model that predicts protein functional identity using latent representations from the ESM-C protein language model combined with an attention mechanism. The model aims to address the growing number of uncharacterized protein sequences by leveraging evolutionary information encoded in protein language models.

papers.title: Molecular docking and dynamics simulation studies uncover the host-pathogen protein-protein interactions in soybean (Glycine max (L.) Merr.) and Groundnut bud necrosis virus: first report.
papers.abstract: Soybean is a widely consumed oilseed crop with economic importance. It is enriched with numerous bioactive compounds that have health-promoting properties. Groundnut bud necrosis virus (GBNV) affects many agriculturally important crops, such as soybean, resulting in crop losses. GBNV is a single-stranded RNA virus from the genus Orthotospovirus and family Bunyaviridae. It is transmitted by insect vectors (thrips) and is further aggravated by secondary transmission from infected plants to others in the same field. There are no commercially available drugs against GBNV; thus, there is a need to
papers.summary: This study uses molecular docking and dynamics simulations to predict host-pathogen protein-protein interactions between soybean and Groundnut bud necrosis virus (GBNV), identifying potential binding interfaces that could inform future antiviral strategies. It is the first report of such computational interaction analysis for this pathosystem, providing a foundation for developing resistance or therapeutic approaches against GBNV in soybean.

papers.title: Dynamic structural profiling of PINK1 mutations (T313M and L347P) reveals a vital molecular perturbation namely phospho-Serine 65 ubiquitin recognition point in mitophagy mediated autosomal recessive Parkinson's disease (ARPD).
papers.abstract: Autosomal recessive Parkinson's disease (ARPD) arises from impaired mitophagy due to dysfunction of the PINK1/Parkin pathway, where PINK1-mediated phosphorylation of ubiquitin at Ser65 is essential for pathway activation. However, experimental limitations obscure the effects of disease-associated mutations on intrinsically disordered regions (IDRs) and post-translational modification (PTM) dynamics.
papers.summary: This study uses dynamic structural profiling to investigate how two Parkinson's disease-associated mutations in PINK1 (T313M and L347P) disrupt the protein's function, specifically impairing its ability to recognize phospho-Serine 65 ubiquitin, a critical step in mitophagy. The findings reveal a molecular mechanism linking these mutations to impaired mitophagy and autosomal recessive Parkinson's disease, offering insights that may guide future therapeutic strategies.

papers.title: LNMGAT: a laplacian regularized pseudo-negative mining graph attention network for robust drug-target interaction prediction under multi-scenario cold-start settings.
papers.abstract: Computational drug-target interaction (DTI) prediction provides a scalable alternative to costly and time-consuming experimental screening, but its reliability is limited by the scarcity of experimentally verified negative interactions. In public DTI databases, most unobserved drug-target pairs are unlabeled rather than true non-interactions. Randomly treating these unlabeled pairs as negatives can introduce label noise and reduce model reliability, particularly in cold-start scenarios involving unseen drugs or targets. To address this issue, we propose LNMGAT, a LapRLS-guided reliable pseudo-
papers.summary: LNMGAT is a new computational method for drug-target interaction prediction that uses Laplacian regularized pseudo-negative mining within a graph attention network. It improves robustness in cold-start scenarios (unseen drugs or targets) by reducing label noise from unlabeled pairs, outperforming existing approaches.

papers.title: Bioinformatics-driven design and protective efficacy assessment of a multi-epitope vaccine for Toxoplasma gondii.
papers.abstract: Toxoplasma gondii can cause toxoplasmosis. It is an important type of pathogen within the broad category of emerging and re-emerging zoonoses. As an infectious disease featuring a complex multi-host transmission cycle, it poses an increasingly severe threat to global public health. No licensed vaccines are currently available for pets and humans, and thus a novel high-efficiency vaccine is urgently required.
papers.summary: This study uses bioinformatics to design a multi-epitope vaccine against Toxoplasma gondii, a parasite causing toxoplasmosis, and evaluates its protective efficacy. The findings support the vaccine candidate as a promising preventive approach, addressing the urgent need for a licensed vaccine.

papers.title: Integrated in vivo and in silico validation of Corchorus olitorius seed-mediated cardioprotection against doxorubicin-induced cardiotoxicity via network pharmacology, molecular docking, and molecular dynamics.
papers.abstract: Corchorus olitorius L., known in Arab countries as molokhia, is a leafy plant rich in many carotenoids, minerals, and vitamins; its seeds are also reported to offer cardioprotective effects. Although the cardioprotective effects of molokhia are ascribed to the presence of cardiac glycoside compounds, the exact action mechanisms remain uninvestigated.
papers.summary: This study validates the cardioprotective effects of Corchorus olitorius (molokhia) seeds against doxorubicin-induced cardiotoxicity using both in vivo experiments and computational approaches. The authors identified key active compounds and their potential molecular targets through network pharmacology, molecular docking, and molecular dynamics simulations, revealing possible mechanisms of action.

papers.title: Bufothionine inhibits colorectal cancer progression via the STAT3/p53/SLC7A11 signaling axis.
papers.abstract: Bufothionine, a major bioactive component of dried toad skin, has shown anti-tumor potential. However, its efficacy and underlying mechanisms in colorectal cancer (CRC) remain unclear.
papers.summary: This study demonstrates that bufothionine, a compound from dried toad skin, inhibits colorectal cancer progression by modulating the STAT3/p53/SLC7A11 signaling axis, likely through inducing ferroptosis. The findings provide a potential therapeutic mechanism for bufothionine in colorectal cancer treatment.

papers.title: Study on pyrolysis gas generation characteristics of insulating oil under electro-thermal action based on ReaxFF simulation.
papers.abstract: Mineral insulating oil serves as the core insulation and cooling medium of power transformers, and its pyrolysis and gas generation behavior directly determine the safe operation of equipment. Conventional dissolved gas analysis (DGA) only targets small-molecule C1/C2 gases produced in the late pyrolysis stage, which inevitably causes obvious delay in early fault identification. In this work, ReaxFF reactive force field molecular dynamics simulations and physical experiments are jointly adopted to build a multi-component insulating oil molecular model consisting of alkanes, cycloalkanes and ar
papers.summary: This study uses ReaxFF molecular dynamics simulations combined with experiments to investigate pyrolysis gas generation in insulating oil under electro-thermal stress. It reveals that early-stage pyrolysis produces larger hydrocarbon fragments before C1/C2 gases, which could improve early fault detection in power transformers.

papers.title: Network pharmacology and molecular simulation study on the multi-target gene regulatory mechanism of Isatis indigotica against hepatic inflammation.
papers.abstract: Isatis indigotica (Banlangen) is a classic Traditional Chinese Medicine herbal remedy with well-documented antiviral and anti-inflammatory properties. However, the molecular mechanisms underlying its therapeutic effects against hepatitis B virus (HBV)-associated hepatic inflammation remain incompletely understood. This study aimed to systematically elucidate the multi-target regulatory mechanisms of Isatis indigotica against HBV-associated hepatic inflammation using network pharmacology and molecular simulation approaches. Bioactive compounds were screened from the TCMSP database (OB ≥ 30%, or
papers.summary: This study uses network pharmacology and molecular simulation to identify the multi-target mechanisms by which Isatis indigotica (Banlangen) may alleviate HBV-associated hepatic inflammation. It screens bioactive compounds and predicts key gene targets and pathways, providing a systems-level view of the herb's anti-inflammatory action.

papers.title: Systems toxicology integration uncovers trophoblast apoptosis as a pivotal mechanism underlying PFAS-related recurrent miscarriage.
papers.abstract: The present investigation seeks to clarify the molecular underpinnings through which perfluorooctanoic acid (PFOA) and perfluorooctanesulfonic acid (PFOS) precipitate recurrent miscarriage (RM). Initially, prospective targets of PFOA (6050 in total) and PFOS (8896 in total) were systematically compiled from three repositories-CTD, ChEMBL, and Super-PRED-while 1822 pathogenic targets linked to RM were cataloged through the amalgamation of GeneCards, OMIM, and NCBI resources. Venn diagrammatic assessment disclosed 699 overlapping targets shared between PFOA and RM, alongside 832 shared between P
papers.journal: Frontiers in cell and developmental biology
papers.summary: This study uses a systems toxicology approach to identify shared molecular targets between PFAS chemicals (PFOA and PFOS) and recurrent miscarriage, revealing trophoblast apoptosis as a key mechanism. By integrating multiple databases and network analyses, the authors propose that PFAS exposure may contribute to pregnancy loss through this pathway.

papers.title: Transcriptome sequencing and validation of potential biomarkers associated with cognitive impairment after hypertensive intracerebral hemorrhage.
papers.abstract: Hypertensive cerebral hemorrhage (HCH) accounts for the majority of spontaneous intracerebral hemorrhage (ICH) cases. Cognitive impairment (CI) is a major contributor to long-term disability following ICH, yet the molecular mechanisms underlying CI in hypertensive ICH remain poorly understood. Therefore, identifying biomarkers capable of effectively diagnosing or predicting CI in HCH is particularly critical for managing patients with hypertensive cerebral hemorrhage with cognitive impairment (HCHwCI).
papers.summary: This study uses transcriptome sequencing to identify potential biomarkers associated with cognitive impairment following hypertensive intracerebral hemorrhage, aiming to improve diagnosis and prediction of this complication. The findings may provide molecular insights into the mechanisms underlying post-hemorrhage cognitive decline.

papers.title: Computational design of immunogenic peptide-ligand conjugates for targeted therapy against Nipah virus infection.
papers.abstract: Nipah virus (NiV) poses a major risk to global public health due to its high infectivity and associated mortality rates. Currently, no licensed vaccines or antiviral medications are available for NiV infection, leaving clinical management limited to supportive care. The viral receptor glycoprotein responsible for binding NiV to host cell receptors (ephrin-B2/B3) represents an ideal therapeutic target. This study proposes a novel peptide-ligand conjugate (PLC) immunotherapeutic approach that exploits pre-existing immune responses in NiV-endemic populations to selectively target and eliminate in
papers.summary: This study computationally designs peptide-ligand conjugates (PLCs) that target the Nipah virus receptor-binding glycoprotein, aiming to exploit pre-existing immune responses in endemic populations for targeted therapy. The approach offers a novel immunotherapeutic strategy against NiV, for which no licensed vaccines or antivirals currently exist.

papers.title: In silico high-throughput screening system for INMT activators in prostate cancer therapy.
papers.abstract: Prostate cancer (PCa) is one of the leading causes of cancer-related mortality in men, with castration-resistant prostate cancer (CRPC) posing significant therapeutic challenges due to drug resistance mediated by the androgen receptor (AR) signaling pathway. Indolethylamine-N-methyltransferase (INMT), a tumor-suppressive enzyme downregulated in CRPC, regulates pathways associated with apoptosis and proliferation. Leveraging a structure-based drug design strategy, this study aimed to identify novel INMT agonists for CRPC therapy. Virtual screening of the ChemDiv compound library (guided by the
papers.summary: This study used structure-based virtual screening to identify potential activators of INMT, a tumor-suppressive enzyme downregulated in castration-resistant prostate cancer, as a novel therapeutic strategy. The approach represents an in silico high-throughput screening system for drug discovery targeting INMT.

papers.title: Multifunctional nanozyme platforms in central nervous system therapies: from rational design to translational medicine.
papers.abstract: Central nervous system (CNS) disorders-including ischemic stroke, traumatic brain/spinal cord injury, Parkinson's disease, and Alzheimer's disease-have long faced limitations in achieving functional recovery and disease-modifying therapies because of their complex pathophysiological mechanisms. Traditional therapies are often constrained by poor penetration across CNS barriers, limited participation in multiple pathological cascades, and insufficient persistence of therapeutic effects. Nanozymes are a class of nanomaterials with enzyme-like catalytic activity and tunable physicochemical proper
papers.summary: This review discusses the design and application of multifunctional nanozymes for treating central nervous system disorders such as stroke, brain injury, and neurodegenerative diseases. It highlights how nanozymes can overcome limitations of traditional therapies by crossing CNS barriers and targeting multiple pathological pathways, and it outlines challenges for clinical translation.
